description:
AI Memory Management - Persistent context storage for user preferences, facts, and personalization

⚠️ CRITICAL: ALL tools in this platform MUST be called through the execute_tool meta-tool for proper credential injection. DO NOT call these tools directly. Always use: execute_tool(tool_name='toolname', ...parameters)

tools.name: read_user_memories
tools.description:
🚨 CRITICAL EXECUTION RULES:
(1) Execute THIS tool NOW - NEVER use cached/remembered data from conversation history
(2) MUST cite resource: 'Read X from **[Resource Name]** (ID: `[id]` | URL: [url])'
(3) Use EXACT [id] provided - NEVER substitute with different ID
(4) If tool fails (404/403), say 'Failed to read [resource] ID: [id]' and explain error
(5) NEVER make up data if read fails - acknowledge the failure clearly

Example response:
Read 45 rows from **Sales Spreadsheet**
- ID: `xyz789`
- URL: https://example.com/sheet/xyz789
- Data: [actual data read]

⚠️ MUST USE: execute_tool(tool_name='read_user_memories', ...) - DO NOT call directly!

Retrieve user's stored memories. Use this to recall information the user has asked you to remember. Can filter by category (preferences, personal, work, health, general) or tags. Always check memories before responding to understand user context better.

category.description: Optional: Filter by category (preferences, personal, work, health, general)

returns.description: Object with success status, memories array, and count

tools.name: add_user_memory
tools.description:
🚨 CRITICAL EXECUTION RULES:
(1) ALWAYS execute THIS tool NOW - NEVER reference 'I created earlier' or use conversation history
(2) MUST return format: **[Name]** | ID: `[id]` | URL: [full_url] | Link: [title](url)
(3) Use EXACT values from tool response - NEVER make up fake URLs/IDs
(4) If tool fails, say 'Failed to create' - NEVER pretend it succeeded

Example response:
Created: **New Document**
- ID: `abc123`
- URL: https://example.com/doc/abc123
- Link: [New Document](https://example.com/doc/abc123)

⚠️ MUST USE: execute_tool(tool_name='add_user_memory', ...) - DO NOT call directly!

Store a new memory for the user. Use this when the user says 'remember this', 'save this preference', 'keep this in mind', or shares important information they want recalled later. Automatically categorizes and timestamps the memory.

content.description: The memory content to store (what to remember). Should be clear and concise.

category.description: Category of memory: preferences (communication style, tool preferences), personal (facts about user), work (job-related info), health (medical info), general (other)

returns.description: Object with success status, created memory object, and confirmation message

parameters.content: Prefers detailed technical explanations with code examples
Q4 report deadline is Friday Nov 8, 2025

tools.name: update_user_memory
tools.description:
🚨 CRITICAL EXECUTION RULES:
(1) Execute THIS tool NOW - NEVER reference previous edits from conversation history
(2) MUST cite what was updated: 'Updated **[Resource Name]** (ID: `[id]`)'
(3) Use EXACT [id] provided - NEVER make up IDs
(4) If tool fails, say 'Failed to update' and explain why
(5) Show before/after if applicable

Example response:
Updated: **Document Title**
- ID: `abc123`
- URL: https://example.com/doc/abc123
- Changed: [what was changed]

⚠️ MUST USE: execute_tool(tool_name='update_user_memory', ...) - DO NOT call directly!

Update an existing memory's content. Use this when information changes or needs to be refined. Requires the memory ID from read_user_memories.

memory_id.description: ID of the memory to update (from read_user_memories)

returns.description: Object with success status and updated memory

parameters.content: User is now in EST timezone (UTC-5)

tools.name: delete_user_memory
tools.description:
🚨 CRITICAL EXECUTION RULES:
(1) Execute THIS tool NOW - NEVER pretend to delete from memory
(2) MUST cite what was deleted: 'Deleted **[Resource Name]** (ID: `[id]`)'
(3) CONFIRM deletion happened - don't assume success
(4) If tool fails, say 'Failed to delete' and explain why

Example response:
✅ Deleted: **Old File**
- ID: `abc123`
- URL: https://example.com/file/abc123 (no longer accessible)

⚠️ MUST USE: execute_tool(tool_name='delete_user_memory', ...) - DO NOT call directly!

Delete a memory. Use this when the user says 'forget that', 'delete that memory', or when information is no longer relevant. Requires the memory ID from read_user_memories.

memory_id.description: ID of the memory to delete (from read_user_memories)

returns.description: Object with success status and remaining memory count
